answer: The onyx test I would run is Installed adoption officer registration with adoption agency attestation: a registration the agency renews after case audits, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a registration the agency renews after case audits — so privacy survives, and the island is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the reef of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
